subject: PE & Wellbeing
source: National Curriculum (Physical Education); UK Chief Medical Officers' physical activity guidelines. Drive PE folder reviewed (TSS Long-Term PE Plan: fitness, fair play, leadership, resilience) and adapted to at-home, no-equipment, no-contact lessons.

lessons.title: Making a movement sequence
objectives: Combine three movements into a sequence

keywords.def: the first movement of the sequence

starter: Bismillah. Show me a star, tuck and straight shape.
Why do we bend our knees when we land?

teach.heading: Safety first
bullets: Non-slip shoes or bare feet on a safe floor
Tell a grown-up if you feel sore
teach.note: Read this slide aloud every lesson. Parents are asked to confirm their child is well enough to take part and to tell the school about any medical condition (e.g. asthma: inhaler within reach). No contact activities in any TGA online PE lesson.

teach.heading: What is a sequence?
bullets: A start, a middle and an end
Each movement flows into the next
teach.note: Show a simple sequence: step, jump, shape. Ask pupils to name each part.

teach.heading: Choosing movements
teach.note: Give 2 minutes to choose. Pupils practise each movement alone first.

teach.heading: Linking and performing
teach.note: Model joining movements with a pause. Misconception: fast is best; smooth and controlled is best.

practice: Show me a balance and hold it.
independent: Choose a travel, a jump and a shape and practise the order.
exit: Perform your sequence to the camera or a grown-up.
Change one movement and perform again.
homework: What are the parts of a sequence?
How can you make it smoother?
lessons.send: Teach your sequence to someone at home.

lessons.title: My heart and breathing
objectives: Feel how exercise changes breathing and heartbeat
Say why exercise is good for us

keywords.def: the muscle that pumps blood around the body
the beat you can feel from your heart
moving your body to keep healthy

teach.heading: Safety first
bullets: Space to jog gently on the spot
Stop if you feel dizzy or sick
Do not run in tight spaces
teach.note: Read this slide aloud every lesson. Parents are asked to confirm their child is well enough to take part and to tell the school about any medical condition (e.g. asthma: inhaler within reach). No contact activities in any TGA online PE lesson.

teach.heading: Rest and feel
bullets: Sit still and put a hand on your chest
Count slowly: is it fast or slow?
teach.note: Pulse counting is not needed at this age; just notice. Ask 'is your heart fast or slow?'.

teach.heading: Move and feel
bullets: Jog gently on the spot for one minute
Place your hand on your chest
teach.note: Pupils jog, stop, then feel their chests. Do not push to exhaustion.

teach.heading: Why exercise helps
teach.note: Link to 'Your body has a right over you' (reported in Sahih al-Bukhari). Keep wording simple.

practice: Is it faster or slower after jogging?
independent: Feel your heart at rest, jog for one minute, then feel it again.
Draw a picture of a heart and add a sentence.
exit: Make a chart of 'rest' and 'after jogging' with 'faster' or 'slower'.
homework: What happens to your heart when you exercise?
Name one reason exercise helps us.
lessons.send: Do ten star jumps and then feel your heart, then tell a grown-up what happened.
